doc.brief: Controls how a widget deals with extra space in a single dimension.
doc.md:
Controls how a widget deals with extra space in a single dimension.

Alignment only matters if the widget receives a “too large” allocation,
for example if you packed the widget with the [`Widget:hexpand`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:hexpand)
property inside a [`Box`](xref:gtk:Box), then the widget might get extra space.
If you have for example a 16x16 icon inside a 32x32 space, the icon
could be scaled and stretched, it could be centered, or it could be
positioned to one side of the space.

Note that in horizontal context `GTK_ALIGN_START` and `GTK_ALIGN_END`
are interpreted relative to text direction.

Baseline support is optional for containers and widgets, and is only available
for vertical alignment. `GTK_ALIGN_BASELINE_CENTER` and `GTK_ALIGN_BASELINE_FILL`
are treated similar to `GTK_ALIGN_CENTER` and `GTK_ALIGN_FILL`, except that it
positions the widget to line up the baselines, where that is supported.

baseline.brief: align the widget according to the baseline.
baseline.md: align the widget according to the baseline.

baseline_center.brief: stretch to fill all space, but align the baseline.
baseline_center.md: stretch to fill all space, but align the baseline.

center.brief: center natural width of widget inside the allocation
center.md: center natural width of widget inside the allocation

end.brief: snap to right or bottom side, leaving space on left or top
end.md: snap to right or bottom side, leaving space on left or top

fill.brief: stretch to fill all space if possible, center if no meaningful way to stretch
fill.md:
stretch to fill all space if possible, center if
  no meaningful way to stretch

start.brief: snap to left or top side, leaving space on right or bottom
start.md: snap to left or top side, leaving space on right or bottom
